title: EC2 in Depth: Storage, Images, and Pricing

questions.prompt: You stop an EC2 instance. What happens to data on its EBS volume versus its instance store?

options.text: EBS data survives; instance-store data is lost
Instance-store data survives; EBS data is lost

questions.explanation: EBS is persistent network storage that survives a stop; instance store is ephemeral and its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates.

questions.prompt: Which workload is the BEST fit for Spot instances?

options.text: A fault-tolerant batch job that can retry if interrupted
A stateful session server that must never restart

questions.explanation: Spot offers deep discounts but can be interrupted with a two-minute warning, so it suits fault-tolerant, stateless, retry-able work — not must-stay-up stateful services.

questions.prompt: Match each EC2 pricing model to what it's best for.

pairs.right: Licensing or compliance needing isolated hardware

questions.explanation: On-Demand is flexible, Savings Plans/Reserved reward steady usage with a discount, Spot is cheap but interruptible, and Dedicated Hosts provide physical isolation.

questions.prompt: What is a custom AMI's scope?

options.text: Global — usable in every Region automatically
Region-scoped — you copy it to other Regions to use it there
Tied to a single instance forever
Only usable in the AZ it was created in

questions.explanation: AMIs are Region-scoped. To launch from an AMI in another Region you copy the AMI there first.

questions.prompt: An application on EC2 obtains temporary AWS credentials from an attached IAM role by querying the instance ____ service.
questions.explanation: The instance metadata service (IMDS, at 169.254.169.254) exposes instance facts and the temporary credentials of the attached IAM role; use IMDSv2 for better security.

options.text: A physical copy of the instance's CPU
An incremental point-in-time backup of a volume, stored in S3
A live mirror that replaces the volume

questions.explanation: A snapshot is a point-in-time backup of an EBS volume kept in S3; after the first full snapshot, later ones store only changed blocks.
